faq.title: The things worth asking first.
faq.description: If something here is unclear, that is our problem to fix, not yours to decode.

included.q: What exactly do I get for the price?
included.a: A finished, deployed build matching the scope you agreed, plus the code and design files. The scope is written down before you pay and is what the price is attached to — that is the whole point of a fixed price.

ownership.q: Do I own what you build?
ownership.a: Yes, entirely. The code, the design and the content are yours on delivery, with no ongoing licence and nothing held back. You can move it to another host or another developer whenever you want, and we will hand over everything needed to do that.

clockStart.q: When does the countdown actually start?
clockStart.a: When your required information and assets are in and the build is officially started — not when you pay. We do not start a clock we cannot control, and you will see the exact start time in your Build Room.

missedDeadline.q: What happens if you miss the deadline?
missedDeadline.a: You choose, not us. Either cancel and take a 100% refund, or let the build continue and take 30% back. It does not require a negotiation and there is no process to argue your way through.

biggerIdea.q: What if my idea is bigger than a 5-Day Build?
biggerIdea.a: The configurator tells you before you pay, and shows which specific capabilities pushed it over — multiple user types, live tracking, multi-party payouts and so on. It then offers the larger build with its own price and timeline, rather than underquoting and renegotiating later.

changes.q: How many changes can I ask for?
changes.a: Changes within the agreed scope are expected and do not affect your delivery date. Changes that add capability are priced as additions, and you will see the figure before anything is built.

hosting.q: Do I have to buy a maintenance plan?
hosting.a: No. You can host it yourself and never pay us again. The plans exist because most people would rather not think about SSL certificates and backups, not because your build stops working without one.

appStores.q: Does the 14 days include App Store approval?
appStores.a: No, and we are explicit about that. We guarantee our development time. Apple and Google control their own review queues and we cannot promise someone else's timeline. Submission and review are tracked separately in your Build Room.

refund.q: How does the refund actually work?
refund.a: It returns to the original payment method, through Stripe, and we start it the same day you choose it. There is no form to fill in and no retention conversation.

different.q: How is this different from hiring an agency?
different.a: An agency sells you a relationship priced by the hour, where the scope and the date move together. This is a product with a published price, a defined scope and a date that costs us money if we miss it. If your project genuinely needs an open-ended engagement, an agency is the right answer and we will say so.

hostingPage.emptyBody: Hosting is recorded when a project goes live.

referralsPage.title: Referrals
referralsPage.subtitle: Who referred whom, what it earned, and what is held back.
referralsPage.emptyBody: A referral appears here when somebody signs up through a link.
referralsPage.flaggedNote: {count} referrals are held for review. Nothing is paid until somebody decides.

partnersPage.title: Partners and affiliates
partnersPage.subtitle: Applications, commission rates and what is owed.
partnersPage.emptyBody: Applications from the partner page appear here.
partnersPage.noCommissionsBody: A commission is raised when a referred build starts.
partnersPage.holdNote: Commissions are held for {days} days after conversion, so a refund cannot leave a paid commission behind.

reviewsPage.title: Reviews
reviewsPage.subtitle: What customers said, and what is published.
reviewsPage.emptyBody: A review appears here once a customer answers an invitation.
reviewsPage.rejectReason: Why it is not being published
reviewsPage.moderationNote: Moderation can reject a review but never edit one. Publishing somebody's words with changes they did not make is worse than not publishing them.

showcasePage.title: Build wall
showcasePage.subtitle: Published builds, and the consent behind each of them.
showcasePage.emptyBody: An entry appears here when a customer agrees their build may be shown.
showcasePage.consentNote: Nothing is published without recorded customer consent, and no customer is named unless they separately agreed to be.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.noneBody: Hosting, updates and monitoring are a separate, cancellable plan.
maintenance.cancelBody: Your plan keeps running until {date}. You have paid for that period and you keep it.
maintenance.upgradeNote: Takes effect now. You will be charged {amount} for the rest of this period.
maintenance.downgradeNote: Takes effect on {date}. Nothing is charged today and nothing is refunded — you keep the plan you paid for until then.
maintenance.pastDueNote: A payment did not go through. Your site stays up while this is sorted out.

credits.title: Build credit
credits.body: Credit is held by you, not by one website. Spend it on any project you own.

billing.title: Billing
billing.lede: Your maintenance plan and your build credit. Both are yours to change at any time.

referral.title: Your referral link
referral.lede: Send it to someone who needs a build. When their build starts, you both get credit.
referral.none: Nobody has used your link yet.
referral.pending: {count} converted and held for review. We check every referral before paying it.
referral.terms: Credit is granted when the referred build officially starts, not when they sign up. Both sides receive the same amount.

reviews.title: How did it go?
reviews.lede: Your build is live. A short, honest review helps the next person decide.
reviews.bodyPlaceholder: What you ordered, how it went, what it does now.
reviews.consentHelp: Without this we keep your review internal. We never publish a name you did not give us.
reviews.sent: Thank you. We read every one.
reviews.notYet: You can review this build once it is live.
reviews.staffBody: Invite the customer to review this build. They can also write one themselves from their Build Room.

showcase.title: Show this build publicly
showcase.body: We would like to put this on our build wall: what it is, what it does, and how long it took. Nothing is published without your say-so, and you can withdraw it at any time.
showcase.consent: Yes, you may show this build
showcase.consented: Thank you. We will write it up and show you before it goes live.
showcase.published: This build is on the wall.
showcase.notLaunched: A build can appear on the wall once it is live.

partners.metaDescription: Refer clients to a platform that ships in days, at a fixed price, with a guarantee.
partners.title: Send your clients somewhere that finishes.
partners.lede: Agencies, freelancers, consultants and advisors refer the builds they do not want to take on. You keep the relationship; we keep the deadline.

apply.title: Apply
apply.body: Tell us who you work with. We read every application.

refer.title: Send a link
refer.body: Approved partners get a referral link and a commission rate.

earn.title: Earn on delivery
earn.body: Commission is earned when the build starts, and released after the refund window closes.

form.title: Apply
form.pitchPlaceholder: The kind of clients you have, and the work you would send our way.
form.sent: Thank you. We will come back to you by email.

tracks.clients: I have clients I would refer

form.audiencePlaceholder: Where you publish, roughly how many people you reach, and why this would suit them.

affiliate.title: Affiliates
affiliate.body: If you have an audience rather than clients, choose the audience track above. It is a separate relationship with its own rate, approved on different grounds.

partners.honest: Commission rates are set per partner when we approve an application. We publish the range rather than a single number because the work an agency does before a referral is not the work an affiliate does.

buildWallPage.metaDescription: Every build that went live, with what it does and how long it took.

invoice.title: Invoice
invoice.languageNote: This invoice was issued in {language} and is shown in that language, as the document of record.
invoice.notFoundBody: This invoice does not exist, or it is not yours. Check the number on your confirmation email.
